app.sources: Air data: Open-Meteo (CAMS model). AQI calculated with the CPCB (India) scale.
app.not_medical: General guidance only, not medical advice.
onb.welcome: Tell us a little about you and we'll turn today's air quality into simple advice that fits your day.
onb.age_sub: Children, older adults and teens breathe in more air for their size, so thresholds differ.
onb.cond_sub: Pick all that apply. This only makes the advice more careful.
onb.privacy: Your profile is saved on this device only.
onb.routine_title: What does your day look like?
onb.routine_sub: Pick all that apply, so tips match how you move around.
onb.loc_sub: We'll show air quality for this place. You can change it any time.

loc.none: No places found. Try another spelling.

hero.approx: Approximate: some pollutants didn't have a full 24 hours of history, so this AQI is an estimate and may differ slightly from official station readings.

catmeaning.moderate: Breathing discomfort for people with lung or heart disease, children and older adults.
catmeaning.poor: Breathing discomfort for most people on prolonged exposure.
catmeaning.severe: Affects healthy people and seriously affects those with existing illness.

mask.n95: Wear a well-fitted N95 / FFP2 mask outdoors.

poll.title: What's in the air
poll.hint: Latest readings. The bar shows each pollutant's AQI score.
why.title: Why this matters
why.p1: The AQI turns several pollutant readings into a single number. It is set by whichever pollutant is worst right now, and in most Indian cities that is PM2.5.
why.p2: PM2.5 particles are about 30 times thinner than a hair. They travel deep into the lungs and can enter the bloodstream, which is why high readings matter even when the air looks clear.
why.p3: Categories follow India's CPCB scale. Children, older adults and people with asthma, COPD or heart disease feel the effects earlier.
